children: equity business continues to be "very strong," but fixed income, currencies, and commodities, or FICC, "has been a little bit softer on a relative basis," CEO and Chairman David Solomon said Wednesday at the Barclays Financial Services Conference.
Still, there are a couple of weeks left to September. "We'll see where that balances out," he added.
Three idiosyncratic factors affecting Q3 are:
Expect a more muted quarter in the investments line after significant activity in Q2
Non-compensation transaction expenses are running higher due to high levels of activity; accelerated tech investments
pulled forward "in a very, very tax-efficient way" a number of years of charitable giving.
As a result, non-comp expenses will be running about $500M higher than in the previous quarter.
provisions for its loan portfolio will be slightly higher this quarter, when compared with the year-ago quarter, due to a couple of idiosyncratic factors, he added.
Solomon noted that overall, activity is strong. Corporate CEO confidence is pretty high. He noted that earnings growth in the S&P 500 is 30% higher than was expected at the beginning of the year.
If Goldman Sachs can deliver 6% revenue growth, Solomon thinks the company can exceed 10% earnings growth.
Technology gives the ability to reimagine profit growth through better efficiency and increase capacity for growth.
While the Goldman chief can't pick the environment, "with a five-to-10-year view, we can continue to grow the company's earnings meaningfully."

He still sees significant opportunities to grow its two main businesses. Even at the same activity level, Solomon sees the opportunity to improve profitability in its banking and markets unit. The company is growing its asset and wealth management business at better than high single digits. "The organic growth in that business is excellent," Solomon said.
